mechanism_narrative: A lower current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its 12-month moving average compresses the discount rate for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month MA is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0 percentage points, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts equity returns: when inflation is high (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and the Fed is not raising rates (FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% in 1 month), the market anticipates a policy response that depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition (CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and FEDFUNDS change < 0.1%), or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, strong housing starts (HOUST above 550,000 units) signal robust consumer demand and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods in the late-cycle expansion regime, or the Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor in this regime falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 90.0, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing and services, reducing corporate earnings and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO < 90.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) relative to its 12-month moving average signals a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when PAYEMS is above its 12-month MA is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0%), high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) exacerbates the negative impact on equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods in the monetary tightening cycle with CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL in this regime falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between labor market strength (PAYEMS growth) and industrial production (INDPRO) predicts equity returns: when employment growth is strong (PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM) and industrial output is contracting (INDPRO < 90.0), it signals a mismatch that reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition (PAYEMS > 0.5% and INDPRO < 90.0), or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
